_comment: Worked example of the curated-pack workflow. It contains only facts already present in the
seed, so loading it changes nothing material - which is the point: it demonstrates the
validation and audit trail without inventing data.
Every load is written to the ingest_log table.
Validation enforced: unknown columns rejected; source_id must exist; fact_status,
confidence and as_of_date are mandatory on every row.

sources.title: NEXTDC Annual / Sustainability Report 2025 (waterless cooling deployment)
sources.notes: Cited by Reuters (23 July 2026) as the source for NEXTDC's statement that it had successfully used waterless direct-to-chip cooling at 50 MW of computing power. Retrieve and read the report itself before elevating any dependent row above REPORTED.

water_profile.drought_response: Not applicable: no evaporative water demand. NEXTDC states it does not plan to use any drinking water for S7.
water_profile.notes: Recycled-water supply was proposed in the April 2026 planning documents, with Sydney Water and coNEXA named as possible suppliers, but talks were abandoned because planning permission for the required pipeline was unavailable. The facility will circulate liquid coolant around the chips and reject heat to air: no water, more energy. NEXTDC's 2025 sustainability report states the same waterless system has cooled 50 MW of computing power elsewhere - one twelfth of the S7 proposal.

metrics.notes: NEXTDC's own reported experience with the waterless direct-to-chip design that S7 will use at 612 MW. The relevant policy question is whether a design proven at 50 MW can be relied on at 12x the scale while still meeting the NSW dPUE ceiling of 1.3.

research_gaps.question: Obtain NEXTDC's measured PUE and WUE for its existing waterless direct-to-chip installation, and compare against the NSW dPUE ceiling of 1.3 for a 612 MW facility in the Western Sydney climate.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: The S7 design change trades water for energy. Without measured numbers the trade cannot be quantified, and the Commonwealth expectation to 'minimise energy demand' cannot be tested against it.
research_gaps.target_source: NEXTDC sustainability reports; NSW Planning Portal S7 EIS once exhibited
